keyVerseText: But when the multitudes saw it, they marvelled, and glorified God, which had given such power unto men.
rootMeaning: The Greek word τοιοῦτος (toioûtos) is formed from the combination of τοί, an enclitic particle used for emphasis or asseveration, and οὗτος, meaning 'this' or 'such.' This etymology reveals that τοιοῦτος literally conveys the idea of 'truly this' or 'of this kind,' emphasizing the character or individuality of the subject. Beyond the simple English gloss of 'such,' the root sense underscores a definitive quality or nature that is being pointed out with certainty.
usageInScripture: With 61 occurrences in the New Testament, τοιοῦτος is predominantly translated as 'such' (32 times), but also appears as 'such things,' 'such an one,' and 'of such,' among others. This range of translations shows that the word is used to denote likeness or a particular kind, whether referring to persons, qualities, or things. Its consistent use to identify or emphasize a specific type or character highlights its role in clarifying the nature of what is being described.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding τοιοῦτος enriches our grasp of biblical descriptions that call attention to the nature or quality of people, actions, or divine attributes. It serves as a linguistic tool to affirm the exactness and reality of what Scripture presents, whether highlighting the power given by God or the character of individuals. This precision in language reflects the biblical emphasis on truth and the particularity of God's work and character. For the Christian faith, it reminds believers to recognize and respond to the genuine and distinct ways God manifests His power and presence in the world.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 9:8, the crowds marvel and glorify God for having given 'such power' to men. The use of τοιοῦτος here emphasizes the remarkable and specific nature of the power bestowed, not just any power but a power of a particular kind that provokes awe and worship. This word draws attention to the extraordinary character of God's gift, encouraging believers to recognize the divine source and quality of the abilities granted to His servants.
